script.title: Intra-State vs Inter-State Supply in GST
script.caption_hook: CGST + SGST or IGST? One simple test decides it

lines.say: Same country, yet CGST and SGST sometimes, IGST other times? How?
Great question! One test decides it: the supplier's location versus the place of supply.
Place of supply? Isn't that just the buyer's billing address?
Not always. For goods, it's generally where delivery ends. The bill address can differ.
Okay, so what happens when both are in the same State?
Then it's intra-state: CGST plus SGST, or UTGST in a Union territory, at equal rates.
A Pune shop delivers a phone to Chennai. Different States, so one tax: IGST.
Wait, what about imports, exports, or SEZ customers?
Imports and exports are always inter-state. Supplies to or by an SEZ are too.
Can IGST credit pay CGST or SGST liability?
Yes. IGST credit pays IGST first, then CGST and SGST in any order. CGST and SGST never cross-set.
Remember: generally, same State splits; apart means IGST. SEZ is always IGST.

check_notes: Writer: Corrected: IGST credit order now IGST first, then CGST/SGST in any order (Sec 49(5) CGST Act, Rule 88A); UT shown as UTGST; SEZ qualifier added to the recap and a list; place of supply for goods now explained (where delivery ends, IGST Act Sec 10). Please confirm the SEZ phrasing (Sec 7(5)(b) IGST Act) and zero-rated export wording.

Checker: Line 13 voice 'SEZ is always IGST' (and Line 10 board 'Export: IGST (zero-rated)'): this suggests IGST is always paid. Supplies to or by an SEZ, and exports, are always INTER-STATE (s.7(5) IGST Act), but they are zero-rated (s.16) and can be made under a LUT/bond without paying IGST (with a refund of unused ITC), or with IGST paid and then refunded. Line 13 fix: 'Supplies to or by an SEZ are always inter-state.' Board fix: 'Export: inter-state, zero-rated (LUT or IGST + refund)'.

Checker: Line 10 'Imports ... are always inter-state': this is right only for the supply in the course of import. Goods count as inter-state until they cross the customs frontier (s.7(2)), and imported services always count as inter-state (s.7(4)). The importer's later domestic sale follows the normal location test. Suggested wording: 'Supplies in the course of import are inter-state.'
